93:  *  LOOKUP_NOEXPIRE: Perform expiration check, but avoid deleting the key,

97:  * still existing, in case this is a replica and the LOOKUP_WRITE is not set.
98:  * Even if the key expiry is primary-driven, we can correctly report a key is
99:  * expired on replicas even if the primary is lagging expiring our key via DELs
100:  * in the replication link. */
101: robj *lookupKey(serverDb *db, robj *key, int flags) {
102:     int dict_index = getKVStoreIndexForKey(key->ptr);
103:     robj *val = dbFindWithDictIndex(db, key->ptr, dict_index);
104:     if (val) {
105:         /* Forcing deletion of expired keys on a replica makes the replica
106:          * inconsistent with the primary. We forbid it on readonly replicas, but
107:          * we have to allow it on writable replicas to make write commands
108:          * behave consistently.
109:          *
110:          * It's possible that the WRITE flag is set even during a readonly
111:          * command, since the command may trigger events that cause modules to
112:          * perform additional writes. */
113:         int is_ro_replica = server.primary_host && server.repl_replica_ro;
114:         int expire_flags = 0;
115:         if (flags & LOOKUP_WRITE && !is_ro_replica) expire_flags |= EXPIRE_FORCE_DELETE_EXPIRED;
116:         if (flags & LOOKUP_NOEXPIRE) expire_flags |= EXPIRE_AVOID_DELETE_EXPIRED;
117:         if (expireIfNeededWithDictIndex(db, key, val, expire_flags, dict_index) != KEY_VALID) {
118:             /* The key is no longer valid. */
119:             val = NULL;
120:         }
121:     }

123:     if (val) {
124:         /* Update the access time for the ageing algorithm.
125:          * Don't do it if we have a saving child, as this will trigger
126:          * a copy on write madness. */

128:             server.current_client->cmd->proc != touchCommand)
